title: Fourteen people, ten berths | चौदह लोग, दस बर्थ (with the take's opening, Saal Bhar)
look: Lugdi pulp cover over a present-day overnight sleeper train: bold black ink outlines, flat red, mustard and night blue, coarse halftone, hard lamp light and deep shadow, the drama of an old paperback cover painted onto today's coach, phones, steel tiffins and plain clothes. Painter rules for every Lugdi panel: no words, letters or numbers anywhere (signs, papers and screens painted blank or shut), unsigned, a plain wall, sky or ceiling above the heads, heads 30 to 45% down, the first speaker in the left third, at most three people, never the player and never anyone from the cards. Papa is only ever seen from behind or heard off the panel; Mausi is painted face-on. The opening (1.01 to 1.06) and the between-chapters page (1.41) are in the present-day household style. Lugdi's big moment, the cover reprint, carries the stamp at 1.37.
goals: Target 1, on Papa's list: 'Berths and meals: on feet 9 hours or more' | 'बर्थ और खाना: 9 घंटे या ज़्यादा खड़े'. Fed by D1 (2 lower berths) and D5 (2 hot plates), the plain Rank twin, set A. Met only at 4 of 4.

Target 2, on Papa's list: 'Cash and first auto: 1 missed train or fewer' | 'पैसे और पहला ऑटो: 1 या कम छूटी ट्रेन'. Fed by D4 (2 cash pouches) and D8 (2 seats in the first auto), the plain Pick a team twin, set B. Met only at 4 of 4.
Fixed line for the 'matters' twin (D2, D6), the same for everyone: 'Tickets: shown. Autos: booked.' | 'टिकट: पास। ऑटो: बुक।'
Stamp on Lugdi's cover reprint: 'At Nani's door: 6:00' (both targets met), '6:30' (one), '7:15' (none). Hard decisions D3 and D7 feed nothing.

beats.painting: Present-day household style, text-free and unsigned, at most two people, heads 30 to 45% down. Early January, first grey light. A phone lies face up on a bedside table, seen a little from above so its screen faces straight out: a plain glowing pale rectangle that fills about two thirds of the panel. A steel water glass beside it, a plain curtain behind. No hand, no body, no shadow. Calm space: the dark wall in the top third. MARKS: [WAITS rulebook Q9: opening on your own phone; if no, Mummy reads the message out from her phone in 1.02].

beats.painting: Present-day household style, text-free and unsigned, at most two people, heads 30 to 45% down. The kitchen. Mummy, 52, plain cotton salwar suit, no bindi or sindoor, stands in the left third, face-on, her right hand pressing a free wall calendar onto a nail: a plain mountain picture over a grid of empty boxes (months and dates are live text). Her left hand holds her shop key ring with a plain brass tag, down at her side. Calm space: the plain pale wall, upper right. No New Year sign or celebration.

The household screen: five present-day portraits laid on as live insets, all one size, over a people-free painting of the same kitchen wall with the new calendar. Quirks are drawn into each portrait's hands, never written: Nani's cane with a rubber foot, Mummy's key ring, Papa's travel list in a clear plastic sleeve, Mama ji's big black umbrella, Tinku's shut scorebook. Portraits checked close up for painted dots and lightened skin. The labels are live text.

HOW RULE 17 WAS READ, for the checker. 'Matched earlier appearances' means the same number of earlier cards, the same mix of top, middle and bottom places, and the same mix of note kinds (plain, judging, heavy). The 'matters' reason counts as plain, and a hard fact counts as heavy. D8's pair matches on those mixes but not place by place: Kiran was top with a heavy fact and low with a judging note, while Prakash was top with a judging note and low with a heavy fact. 'Weakest' means a card that every other card beats or equals on both numbers. The only one in the chapter is Mehul at D8, the last decision. If the checker ranks by the two numbers' total instead, the bottom is a tie of two or more in D1 to D7, and the tie includes people in later pairs at D1 to D5.
RULE 15: no tie between two women or two men in chapter 1. The rulebook asks for them from chapter 2 on, and the options file wanted them here too. Adding one breaks rule 17 in this circle.

HINDI FOR A NATIVE READER (rule 66; none is a future or a past tense about you). These lines were flagged and only a reader can clear them: 'सब तुम्हें ही फ़ोन करते हैं' (the subject is सब), the 'who should' asks रखे?, जाए?, करे? and मिले?, 'एक सीट ख़ाली' and 'एक बेंच ख़ाली' (the seat and the bench), 'नानी ने चाय गरम रखी' (Nani), 'बेटी की शादी' (Mama ji's daughter), 'स्कोर मेरा' (Tinku), and the polite लिस्ट दिखाइए, पेन दीजिए and चलिए said by you. Five Hindi-first readers also check that 'पिछले सफ़र में अजनबी पीछा करता रहा' (Kiran) and 'एक बार प्लेटफ़ॉर्म पर कोई उसके पीछे लगा रहा' (Chetan) weigh the same (rule 28), and that नखरे and शरमाती or झिझकता sound like loaded words.

Vivek sells seeds, Mehul drives a milk van and Hetal teaches maths, which fit type. Kiran's bank job fits neither.
